Background reading and **reference material** the workshop's chapters cite into — single-cell biology, statistics, shell scripting, Git, databases, file formats, and a methods-section template. Read what you need, when you need it.

These materials support the core workshop but are not part of the three-day sequence — they're linked from **[Additional Resources](../Additional_Resources.html)**. Quick one-page references (R, Seurat, ggplot2, SLURM, Git…) are on the separate **[Cheat Sheets](../Cheat_Sheets.html)** tab.

::: callout-note
**Getting up and running (R, the command line, computers & HPC).** That material is now the two **Day 0 modules** — work them before the workshop if any of it is rusty:

- [Day 0 · Module 1 — Computer System Fundamentals](Chapter_Day0_1_Computer_Systems.html) — how computers, operating systems, and HPC clusters work; UO's Talapas (accounts, login, modules, SLURM); VS Code + Remote-SSH; reproducible environments (`renv` / Docker / Apptainer).
- [Day 0 · Module 2 — R & the Command Line](Chapter_Day0_2_R_and_CommandLine.html) — shell navigation, pipes & redirection; R, RStudio, data structures, functions, packages, the tidyverse.
:::

## Appendices — reference material

Listed in the order they tend to come up across the workshop flow.

| # | Appendix | Topic |
|---|---|---|
| C | [Single-Cell Biology Refresher](Appendix_C_SC_Biology_Refresher.html) | The molecular biology behind scRNA-seq — read this before Lecture 00 if your bio is rusty |
| D | [Statistical Foundations](Appendix_D_Statistical_Foundations.html) | NB / Poisson, design matrices, FDR, shrinkage, why per-cell tests fail |
| F | [GREP, Regular Expressions & Shell Scripting](Appendix_F_GREP_Regex_Shell.html) | Pattern matching with `grep`, regex syntax, writing reusable shell scripts |
| G | [Git, GitHub & Version Control](Appendix_G_Git_GitHub.html) | Tracking changes with Git, collaborating on GitHub, common workflows |
| I | [Gene-Expression Databases & File Formats](Appendix_I_Databases_FileFormats.html) | The big-six scRNA-seq repositories and a field guide to every file format |
| J | [Common Bioinformatics File Formats](Appendix_J_Bioinformatics_File_Formats.html) | A field guide to FASTA, FASTQ, SAM/BAM, GFF3/GTF, BED, VCF, BigWIG, and the single-cell containers — with annotated head-of-file examples |
| K | [Methods-Section Template](Appendix_K_Methods_Template.html) | Annotated boilerplate for an scRNA-seq paper's methods section |

The **[Glossary](Glossary.html)** of single-cell terminology is at the top of the [Additional Resources](../Additional_Resources.html) page; read it alongside the lectures.

## How to use these resources

::: callout-tip
**Read on demand.** The workshop [chapters](../Materials.html) cross-reference these liberally — when a chapter says "see Appendix D § 8 for why per-cell DE fails", that's a hint to read that section before continuing.

**If you're new to the toolchain:** start with the two [Day 0 modules](../Materials.html) (R, the command line, computers & HPC) before Day 1.

**If your molecular biology is rusty:** Appendix C, before Lecture 00.

**If your statistics is rusty:** Appendix D, before Lecture 05 / Chapter 5.

**Once you start writing up your own scRNA-seq results:** keep Appendix K (Methods-Section Template) open in another tab.
:::
